summary: Toronto Community Housing Corporation is Canada’s largest landlord. In 2016, City Council approved shifting Toronto Community Housing Corporation to be a landlord of excellence. In the last four years, the City of Toronto has shown its commitment to the residents of Toronto Community Housing Corporation by significantly funding the state of good repair program and increasing their subsidy by 16 percent so that residents can rely on their elevators and live comfortably in their homes. While work has progressed on realigning Toronto Community Housing Corporation to be more tenant focused and responsive, it has not moved fast enough. In 2017, City Council unanimously approved Tenants First, an ambitious project that would see the seniors housing units under a new governance model wherein they can effectively partner with health service institutions to provide the necessary services for seniors to age comfortably in place. This would allow better service to be provided to seniors and allow Toronto Community Housing Corporation to have laser like focus on its core tenants being individuals, families, and the vulnerable. Furthermore, there are other services within Toronto Community Housing Corporation's corporate structure that are not identified in Tenants First that should be given consideration for synergies with the City. City Council direct the City Manager to report to the Executive Committee on March 21, 2019 on: a. accelerating the Tenants First Project; b. synergies between Toronto Community Housing and City divisions; and c. any governance changes required to accomplish Parts 1.a and 1.b above.
